# GameSpot — contemporary review

- Original source: [GameSpot — contemporary review](https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood-review/1900-2897317/)
- Author / publication: Brett Todd / GameSpot
- Language / date: English; 2002-11-12
- Access: Live page blocked (HTTP 403); text read from the Wayback Machine capture
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09, from the 2024-12-03 capture
- Archived copy: [Wayback Machine, 2024-12-03](https://web.archive.org/web/20241203143258/https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood-review/1900-2897317/)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial review, not transcribed)

**Score: 8.6/10.**

Todd praises the story, varied mission objectives, and mouse-directed combat. He describes Sherwood as an active headquarters where individual Merry Men manufacture supplies, train, and recover before the player chooses a mission and party.

The campaign alternates compact forest ambushes with larger town and castle operations. The review values the game's romantic interpretation of Robin Hood and its atmospheric presentation. Animated scenery, detailed backgrounds, and environmental sounds help make the towns and forest feel inhabited.

Criticisms include dated production values, repeated voice lines, and limited additional modes: the reviewed release has no multiplayer, skirmish mode, or mission editor.

**Research use:** a positive launch-era assessment of campaign structure, usability, and atmosphere. Statements about missing features refer to the reviewed original release.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: by Brett Todd, 12 November 2002 4:45PM PST; score 8.6 "Great"; deck line says story, mission design and combat system combine so the game "works on nearly every level". Commercial review, so paraphrased.

- Positioning: German developer Spellbound; blends the Kevin Costner and Errol Flynn films with Commandos-style real-time tactics; only significant complaints are no multiplayer and dated production values.
- Structure: third-person isometric; two solo opening missions introduce the engine and first allies; then a tree-house headquarters in Sherwood that works like an RTS base with huts as small factories, except everything is made manually by assigning men to workshops (arrows, leather for purses); training with a drill instructor and tree-mounted targets; apples gathered under a tree; meat at the spit; feast table restores health.
- Map lists Sherwood and five districts: Lincoln, Nottingham, Derby, York, Leicester. Multiple missions usually available. Two categories: forest-road convoy ambushes (set pieces with traps triggered by shooting targets in trees, pits, men hidden under leaves) and town expeditions with explicit goals (find Marian, contact Prince John); beggars sell hints for alms.
- Castle sieges: need 12 shields before the assault, earned by paying allies, sending Merry Men on spying patrols, or looting a convoy; more shields during the fight for tasks such as lowering the drawbridge.
- Enemies: lancers up to mounted knights and officers who organise troops; Alt shows one soldier's vision cone at a time; awareness colour-coded green, yellow, red; enemies fetch reinforcements or an officer when outnumbered or on seeing a body; civilians panic and alert guards.
- Difficulty: remarkably hard even on easy; intricate maps. Abilities: Robin throws purses or knocks out; Will Scarlet strangles; Stutely ties up. Generic types: aggressive (close combat and healing), strong (carry bodies, whistle), mustachioed (archers, weak in melee).
- Combat: click enemy to attack, click self to block, click-and-drag for special moves following the sword edge (sideways thrust, figure eight); bow is automatic. Recruitment depends on lives spared.
- Extras: no multiplayer, skirmish or editor. Graphics: hand-drawn 2D sprites and backgrounds with swaying foliage, running water, chimney smoke, animated clothing; combatants slide down stairs step by step when knocked out. Sound: location-specific ambient samples (birds, bees in camp); limited voice lines, with one Robin kill line heard about one time in three; slight music.
